goal: The delivered research report reads as a professional document a person could hand off as-is: organised around the reader's purpose (for a buyer, an inspection checklist and failure modes by subsystem), with one honest limitations section and no blocks addressed to the model; the accuracy and citation discipline of the current output are kept unchanged. When the first pass leaves needs open, the engine runs one bounded gap-closing pass BEFORE delivering, tells the reader in the chat that it is doing so, and the final document recommends a further run only for what is still open after that.
artifact: Patch to OB1/integrations/research-service/templates.ts (purpose-driven templates incl. a buyer's-guide/checklist template with a subsystem table; template selection uses answered+partial needs, not answered alone), report.ts + lib.ts renderResult + owui/tools/deep_research.py fallback (one Limitations/Open questions section derived from the [GAP] lines and needs_status, replacing the duplicated 'What was not found' + 'Open gaps' blocks; the INCOMPLETE directive to the model moved out of the human-facing body into a short trailing machine line; the async hand-off notice removed from the final message by the callback), and the coverage judge (a need with >= 2 grounded [SOURCED]/[INFERRED] lines counts as answered, so 7 concrete findings never print as 'answered 0 of 7'); tests RED->GREEN; TEST-PLAN with the live OptiPlex chat run as the proof. Plus harness.ts: a bounded automatic gap-closing pass on the topic path (one extra gather+synthesis round targeting the [GAP]/open needs, within the job's wall clock, counted and shown in the footer), and the async callback writing an interim status into the chat message ('First pass: X of N needs answered - running a gap-closing pass') before the final rewrite.
audience: The operator handing the report to a colleague who did not run it and will not read the engine's record; they need the answer, the checklist, the evidence, and the limits, in that order.
acceptance: Re-rendering the recorded synthesis of job 33250e9b (documentation/evidence: the live OptiPlex run) produces a document with: a title stating the finding; an executive summary; a 'What to check in person' checklist for the buyer; a failure-modes-by-subsystem table (PSU, socket, RAM, BIOS, thermal, capacitors) each row cited; ONE limitations section listing open questions once; a numbered Sources list; and no text addressed to the model in the body.

The footer states needs answered consistently with the body: the 33250e9b synthesis renders as at least 'answered 5 of 7', not '0 of 7 (7 partly)'; a synthesis with no grounded line for a need still shows that need open.

The 'Open gaps' block and the 'What was not found' section never both appear; the INCOMPLETE directive appears only as a single trailing line prefixed for the model (e.g. '<!-- engine: ... -->' or a one-line italic), verified byte-identical between lib.ts and deep_research.py.
The async callback rewrites the message so the final chat body starts with the report title, not with 'Research is running in the background'; verified on a live OWUI run.

Template selection: a run whose answered+partial needs are >= 3 is classified into a purpose template (buyer's guide, scientific paper, technical doc...); the classifier is given the QUESTION's purpose (buy / build / learn / compare) and the general template is the fallback only when nothing fits.

Every [Source N] citation in the rendered document resolves to the same source it did in the tagged synthesis (renumbering test); no new fact, number or URL appears in the rendered document that is not in the synthesis (grounding diff test on 33250e9b).
deno test -A in research-service stays green with at least 203 passed; the 100 Hz dry run still cites PMC11955832 after deploy.

When the first synthesis leaves any need open or partial and wall-clock budget remains, the run performs exactly one gap-closing pass: queries derived from the open needs, new sources gated and screened like round 1, a re-synthesis over the merged pool; the footer shows 'gap-closing pass: +K sources, needs answered X of N -> Y of N'. A mocked run asserts the pass runs once, never twice, and not at all when every need is answered or the wall clock is exhausted.

On the async path the chat message is rewritten TWICE: an interim body 'First pass complete: X of N needs answered - running a gap-closing pass to close the rest' when the pass starts, then the final document; verified on a live OWUI run by reading the message between the two writes.

The final document's limitations section names what is still open after the gap-closing pass and, when anything is, ends with one sentence recommending a further targeted run in the reader's terms; when nothing is open it says the question is answered and omits the recommendation.
The gap-closing pass never persists claims from an intermediate synthesis: the curator is delegated to once, with the final merged synthesis; a test asserts one delegateToCurator call.
out_of_scope: Search, entity gate, curator, engine policy - unchanged.
Source weighting for which finding leads the title (separate item).
Any change to what is stored in Open Brain.
Multiple automatic passes or unbounded time; the digest/article path (untouched).
